Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the draft order form. Procurement has two housekeeping asks before we can route for PO approval:

1) Invoicing entity — the order form currently lists "Redwood Inference, Inc. (US)" but our finance org requires invoices from a US entity registered to accept VAT/withholding documentation. Can you confirm the legal entity that will appear on the invoice and whether Redwood will accept our UK VAT and US tax withholding certificates?

2) Minimum commit phasing — Acme prefers to split the first-year commit into two tranches (60% on signing / 40% at six months) rather than a single upfront prepayment. We need an invoice cadence and whether we can receive two invoices tied to deliverables so our AP team can schedule payment.

3) Net terms — our standard is Net 45 once invoiced. Is Redwood able to accommodate Net 45 for this account? If not, please confirm the shortest term you can provide.

Attached is a redline from our procurement counsel highlighting the invoicing entity clause and tax flow. Please advise asap — our PO lead is on a tight deadline for the quarter close.

Thanks,
Sandra

Sofia / Ben / Sandra —

Quick legal/finance summary after review with RevRec:

1) Invoicing entity: Confirmed — Redwood Inference, Inc. (US) is the correct bill-to/legal entity for hosted service invoices. We will populate the US Tax ID and remit address on the invoice. Acme's AP can route the invoice against that entity.

2) Tax withholding: Redwood cannot accept unilateral withholding by the customer unless there is a written tax treaty or offset arrangement. We will accept country-specific VAT registration information and will issue VAT invoices where applicable, but any withholding at source must be pre-approved and explicitly documented. If Acme intends to withhold for US tax reasons, we need a formal certificate and an explicit clause in the order form that states responsibility and any gross-up obligations. Suggested wording (for your counsel):

"Customer shall be responsible for any taxes, duties or withholdings imposed on payments hereunder. If Customer withholds amounts from payments, Customer must (i) provide Redwood with official documentation supporting the withholding and (ii) pay such amounts grossed-up so that Redwood receives the full amount due under this Order Form."

3) Payment cadence / revenue recognition: RevRec is OK with a 60/40 split on the first-year commit provided the order form ties each tranche to a clear billing event (e.g., "Invoice #1: on execution — 60% of Year 1 Commitment; Invoice #2: six months post-execution — 40%"). We will need the order form to reference invoice numbers and expected delivery dates so accounting can time-recognize revenue.

4) Net terms: Finance will approve Net 45 for ACME as a one-year concession. This will appear as an exception in the payment terms appendix and flagged for review at renewal.

Next steps:
- Ben: please incorporate the revised payment schedule and the suggested tax withholding paragraph into the order form redline.
- Sandra: if you can confirm the PO approver's name and whether Acme's AP will accept two separate invoice numbers, Legal can include the exact gross-up clause language in the final redline.

I attached a PDF with inline redlines on your original order form (ACME_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf).
